clue.text: Jack in turn got rid of what is discoloured

parts.note: a jack tar, or simply a tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: turn tells us the little word in is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
to shed something is to cast it off or get rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone throws away whatever has gone dull or stained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like 'by turns' but turns IN round to NI, which sits between TAR and SHED; 'what is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver that has lost its shine through oxidation is described as dulled or stained in exactly this way.

clue.text: They make fast changes of course

explanation.surface: Something that both fastens things and alters direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pins fasten cloth or carpet, and a sailing boat zigzagging into the wind alters heading with each manoeuvre.

clue.text: He 'would not be deceived about a catalogue

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand meaning concerning
a list is an itemised catalogue

explanation.surface: A shrewd man refuses to be fooled by a sales catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-headed person who sees things as they are cannot easily be fooled.

clue.text: Mix-up of fifty in one big room.

definitions.text: Mix-up of fifty in one big room.

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Fifty people crammed into a single hall produce chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: fifty people in one hall make a muddle. The Roman numerals L and I join BIG ROOM to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian loan word for a confused, embarrassing entanglement or tangled situation.

clue.text: Craftsmen who know how to deal with strikers.

definitions.text: Craftsmen who know how to deal with strikers.

parts.words: Craftsmen who know how to deal with strikers.
parts.note: strikers suggests industrial action, but here they are clocks that chime the hours, and these craftsmen repair timepieces

explanation.surface: Skilled tradesmen who can handle workers on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock and watch makers study the science of measuring time and mend chiming timepieces.

clue.text: Restrain a crazy uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Hold back a wild revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier across a river holds water back, so to restrain is a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: Palindromic performances

indicators.note: the defining word reads the same forwards and backwards, which is all the wordplay offers

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: Pieces played or sung by one artist alone are single-voice performances.

clue.text: Charming woman adds point to royal, address

parts.note: Sire is the old form of address to a king
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An alluring woman adds a final touch to a speech to the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adds ... to' places N after SIRE; the comma after 'royal' is an OCR stray, the page prints 'royal address'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these sea creatures lured sailors with song, hence a seductive woman.

clue.text: One spotted by Pope and partner

parts.note: Leo is the name of many popes
pard is old American slang for partner

explanation.surface: Someone noticed by the Pope and his companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is famous for the dark rosettes on its coat.

clue.text: Dan 'says it 'might be December. 26th, for example

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan reckons it could be Boxing Day.
explanation.walkthrough: December 26th is St Stephen's Day, a feast of a saint; the stray apostrophes and full stop are OCR marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts in the church calendar honour individual holy figures, as December 26th honours Stephen.

clue.text: Charles essaying to turn about to make the difficult climb

annotationWithheld.why: Charles essaying to turn about to make the difficult climb: LAMB (Charles the essayist) gives the middle, but no reading supplies both C and ER without 'about' doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Charles essaying to turn about to make the difficult climb

clue.text: Polo in Islington area for a man of invention

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller
N1 is the London postal district covering Islington, read as the letters NI

explanation.surface: A game of polo played in a north London district by an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a district of north London whose postcode is N1, here read as NI after MARCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered radio telegraphy, so he is a famous inventor.

clue.text: Sounds like a cunning move in Ireland

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase, when spoken, gives the answer's sound

parts.note: sly means cunning and a go is a move or turn

explanation.surface: A crafty manoeuvre made somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county and town on the north-west coast of the Irish republic.

clue.text: Prepare an ambush, like the untruthful slimmer, say.?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: a dieter who fibs about the scales would lie in weight

explanation.surface: A dishonest dieter plotting an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding to attack someone by surprise means waiting in concealment for a victim.

clue.text: Abolition of gin tax?.Tripe! Possible, though

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words could possibly be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of scrapping the duty on gin, yet admits it could happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The gerund serves as a noun: rooting something out is its abolition.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out completely is to destroy or wipe out entirely, as in uprooting a plant.

clue.text: The Cheshire variety slowly disappeared

parts.note: the Cheshire one in Alice in Wonderland fades away until only its grin is left

explanation.surface: A Cheshire cheese gradually vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's grinning creature fades away until only its smile remains.

clue.text: Soviet official puts young girl into deep, sleep, right ?

indicators.note: the girl is put into the sleep, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconscious sleep
a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A party functionary sends a young woman into a deep sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A Communist Party officer in the USSR, especially one overseeing political loyalty.

clue.text: Unsteady as a lamp-post

explanation.surface: Wobbling about like a street lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness makes a person feel faint, and a street lamp literally has an illuminated top.

clue.text: Active citizen, for example a Frenchman, rises

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the whole run is read from the bottom up

parts.note: cit is a short form of citizen
Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A busy townsman, a Frenchman for instance, gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and vigorous people are full of energy.

clue.text: Interpret wrongly truisms once distorted

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Familiar sayings, once twisted, get misread.
explanation.definitionFit: To misread or misunderstand something is to take its meaning the wrong way.

clue.text: Misery of deans adrift in a ship

indicators.note: the jumbled deans go inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: drifting loose, so the letters of deans are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unhappy clergy cast loose on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappiness and sorrow are the same state of mind as misery.

clue.text: That pen is an eyesore !

explanation.surface: A pigsty is an ugly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen keeps pigs, and the same sound spelt with an E is an eyelid inflammation, a sore on the eye.

clue.text: In ecstasy, ring a ring of lilac

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Joyful dancers circle round a lilac bush, as in a nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring of' is padding that echoes the nursery rhyme 'Ring-a-ring o' roses'.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name for the common garden shrub with scented spring flowers.

clue.text: Aids one in reorganizing : the islands

indicators.note: putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Help arrives in restructuring an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian nation is an archipelago of thousands of islands.

clue.text: Observes the music

explanation.surface: Someone watches the sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark or take notice is one sense; written musical symbols on a stave are the other.

clue.text: Blush like this matador ?

explanation.surface: A bullfighter turns crimson.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn crimson is to flush, and a bullfighter tossed on the horns has been pierced.

clue.text: Many placed behind are gloomy

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
the rear is the back or behind

explanation.surface: Crowds pushed to the back are miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and cheerless, a poetic word for dreary.

clue.text: Suspected by nosy Parker ?

explanation.surface: Something a busybody guessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensing something is to detect it, and a busybody, a nosy Parker, detects things with the nose.

clue.text: Sounds like money for the tonic

indicators.note: the word for money, when spoken, gives the musical note

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash spent on a refreshing drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the first note of the scale, the keynote, is named this.

clue.text: Concentrated in the past for instance

parts.note: the past is one grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone who was focused in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and concentrated feeling or flavour is fierce and extreme.

clue.text: Flung by a lover, faithful in his fashion

definitions.text: Flung by a lover, faithful in his fashion

parts.words: Flung by a lover, faithful in his fashion
parts.note: Ernest Dowson's poem Cynara has a lover who flung flowers riotously yet was faithful in his fashion

explanation.surface: Something thrown by a lover who stays true in his own way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowson's poet flung blooms riotously with the throng, the flowers of love.

clue.text: Exalted professorship re served for the baby.

parts.note: high means exalted or lofty
a chair is a university professorship

explanation.surface: A senior academic post set aside for an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 're served' is the OCR split of 'reserved', a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants sit in a tall seat with a tray to be fed at table.
